title: Connectivity and digitalisation for clean and affordable energy
summary: Find out more about Connectivity and digitalisation for clean and affordable energy, don't miss it.
body_markdown:
Once again, world leaders are gathering at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to take stock of the progress achieved and address the challenges that remain. For the first time, the summit has two host countries, Türkiye and Australia, which share a strategic priority: energy.


In this context, both countries have made a joint commitment through the “[35-by-35 Global Electrification Initiative](https://cop31.tr/assets/docs/action-agenda/cop31-global-electrification-concept-note.pdf) ”, which sets a target for electricity to account for 35% of final energy consumption by 2035. The initiative seeks to strengthen the role of electricity in the global energy system by accelerating the uptake of electric vehicles, heat pumps, clean industrial technologies and renewable electricity, while reducing dependence on fossil fuels.


In this context, Telefónica is helping to advance the energy transition through its connectivity and digital solutions, supporting countries in meeting their objectives. To this end, we are publishing a new Policy Brief that highlights the role of the sector in this transformation and sets out recommendations to fully harness its enabling potential.


### Policy Brief: Connecting the energy transition


- [Connecting the energy transition. Policy Brief 2026 PDF | 5 MB](https://www.telefonica.com/en/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2026/11/ENG-Policy-Brief-Transicion-Energetica_V2-1.pdf)


## Connectivity and digitalisation: driving the energy transition


Transforming the energy system is essential to decarbonise the economy and strengthen energy autonomy in the face of high external dependence. Moving towards a cleaner, more flexible and integrated model requires not only changing how we produce and consume energy, but also managing an increasingly complex, decentralised and dynamic system.


In this process, connectivity and digitalisation play an essential role as enablers of the energy transition, facilitating more efficient coordination across electricity generation, distribution and consumption. Telecommunications networks, together with technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence and edge computing, make it possible to monitor and manage energy flows in real time, thereby delivering greater efficiencies.


First, the growing integration of renewable energy requires more dynamic management of the electricity system because of the variability of renewable generation and the need to maintain a balance between supply and demand. In this context, smart grids, supported by connectivity and digital solutions, can anticipate imbalances and optimise electricity distribution. In parallel, artificial intelligence can improve renewable-generation forecasts and anticipate potential peaks, enabling more efficient production and management.


Second, the electrification of homes, industry and transport is transforming the traditional energy model. As renewable self-consumption expands, consumers can also produce, store and exchange energy, giving rise to an increasingly decentralised and bidirectional system. In addition, the integration of millions of new distributed resources, such as electric vehicles, batteries and heat pumps, increases the complexity of energy management and requires greater coordination. Connectivity and digitalisation are therefore essential.


Finally, electrification must be accompanied by continuous improvements in energy efficiency, so that the increase in electricity demand associated with this process is managed in a way that reduces the energy required to carry out the same activity.


## Towards a connected and intelligent energy future


Despite the role of connectivity and digitalisation in the energy transition, their contribution is still not sufficiently recognised. To place them at the heart of the energy-transition implementation agenda, Telefónica proposes the following recommendations:


– Recognise connectivity and digitalisation as enablers of global electrification, renewable-energy integration and energy-efficiency objectives.


– Mobilise public and private financing for projects that integrate the ICT sector, digitalisation and connectivity into the energy transition and/or electrification. Recognise the green and sustainable attributes of these initiatives through sustainable-finance frameworks that include these technologies on the basis of their environmental impact.


– Include cybersecurity and resilience among the eligible financing categories for the digitalisation of energy grids and assets, protecting the monitoring, remote-control and communications systems associated with critical infrastructure and services.


– Ensure that the digital energy transition is fair and inclusive by extending connectivity and digital capabilities to rural areas and vulnerable groups, so that lack of digital access does not become a new barrier to electrification. The COP31 agenda notes that around 730 million people still lack access to electricity.


Greater integration of connectivity and digitalisation into the energy transition will help expand renewable generation, optimize the management of the energy system to facilitate electrification, and improve energy efficiency. This will advance decarbonisation, strengthen domestic energy-production capacity and support more affordable energy for the benefit of society.
